topics.title: CSS-in-JS performance. MUI's sx prop trade-offs.
topics.html:
• MUI v5: Emotion — CSS-in-JS with runtime class generation. Costs runtime CPU and SSR hydration overhead.
  • MUI v6+ Pigment CSS: zero-runtime, statically extracted at build. Performance closer to CSS Modules.
  • sx prop: convenient for one-off overrides. For hot paths (tables, lists) prefer styled() or CSS Modules.
💬 Say it like this

CSS-in-JS is convenient because styles live next to the component, but with Emotion the class names are generated at runtime, so it costs CPU on every render and adds work during hydration.

The sx prop is fine for one-off overrides. In hot paths like tables and long lists I prefer styled() or CSS Modules, or a zero-runtime solution where styles are extracted at build time.

topics.title: Design tokens — what are they and how to set up in MUI?
topics.html:
const theme = createTheme({
  palette: { primary:{ main:"#5B4BE0",light:"#7B6FE8",dark:"#3D30B8" }, brand:{subtle:"#F0EDFF",emphasis:"#3C3489"} },
  shape: { borderRadius: 8 },
});
declare module "@mui/material/styles" {
  interface Palette { brand: { subtle: string; emphasis: string } }
}
💬 Say it like this

Tokens are named design values — colours, spacing, radius — instead of hard-coded numbers in components. In MUI they live in the theme, and I extend the theme types with module augmentation so custom tokens are type-safe.

The benefit is that a redesign or a dark theme is a change in one file, not a search across the whole codebase.

topics.title: CSS Cascade Layers (@layer) and specificity.
topics.html:
/* Specificity: */
#nav .link:hover /* (1,1,1) */   .nav a.active /* (0,2,1) */
style="color:red" /* inline — higher than any selector */
@layer base, components, utilities;
@layer base { button { background: white; } }
@layer utilities { .bg-primary { background: #5B4BE0; } }
/* utilities ALWAYS wins over base regardless of specificity */
💬 Say it like this

Cascade layers let me decide the order of my styles explicitly. I declare layers like base, components and utilities, and a later layer always wins over an earlier one, no matter how specific the selector is.

That removes the usual specificity war — no more !important just to override a library style.

topics.title: Flexbox vs Grid — when which?
topics.html:
• Flexbox: one-dimensional (row OR column). Component-level layout — toolbars, button rows, nav.
  • Grid: two-dimensional (rows AND columns). Page-level layout — sidebars + main + footer, card grids.
  • Combine: Grid for page structure, Flex inside each grid cell.
💬 Say it like this

Flexbox is for one direction — a row or a column. Grid is for two directions at the same time, rows and columns together.

In practice I use Grid for the page structure, like sidebar plus content, and Flexbox inside the blocks, for toolbars or button rows.
